name: Compaq Computer Corporation

summary.text: Compaq Computer Corporation was a Houston-based computer maker. In 1999 it bought two internet companies to build out its AltaVista search portal: Shopping.com, acquired on February 15, 1999 for about $257 million, and Zip2 Corporation, for which it announced a definitive cash agreement on February 16, 1999 and completed the purchase in April 1999 at an aggregate price of about $341 million, including $307 million in cash. Zip2 was folded into AltaVista.

facts.claim: Compaq announced on February 16, 1999 a definitive agreement to acquire Zip2 Corp. for cash, buying all outstanding shares with the unanimous approval of Zip2's board, and completed the acquisition by cash tender offer in April 1999, announcing completion on April 5, 1999.
facts.quote: A Compaq release dated February 16, 1999 said it had reached a definitive agreement to acquire Zip2 Corp. The deal was a cash purchase of all outstanding shares, and Zip2's board had unanimously approved it.

facts.claim: Compaq's 1999 annual report records the Zip2 purchase at a total aggregate price of $341 million, comprising $307 million in cash, employee stock options valued at $28 million and other costs; AltaVista's S-1 gives $340.9 million ($307.2 million cash, options with a fair value of $27.7 million). The $307 million figure widely cited is the cash component.

openQuestions: The brief describes Compaq as 'flush with bubble cash'. The filings retrieved show the Zip2 and Shopping.com purchases were cash deals but say nothing about Compaq's cash position or the source of funds; Compaq's 1999 10-K balance sheet would show this.
The site's entity index lists a separate 'Compaq Board' (compaq-board) entity; no source retrieved this session names Compaq directors in connection with the Zip2 deal.
CMGI's 1999 Form 8-K/A filings (on CMGI's later purchase of a majority of AltaVista from Compaq) appeared in search results but their content was not retrieved.
